characters.description: An engineer and independent software-company owner who has sold his business and secured his finances. Still affected by a recent breakup, he arranges postmortem cryonic preservation.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: Bob's trainer and liaison after his return to awareness in 2133. He explains that Bob is a software mind produced by a destructive scan, that the biological man is gone, and that the new Bob is property competing for an undisclosed assignment. Failure may result in storage, reconditioning, or destruction.
characters.name: Dr. Landers

characters.description: Bob's ship-style system interface, responsible for relaying status information, computational feedback, and details about remote machinery. Guppy helps Bob learn to coordinate multiple roamers through broad instructions rather than constant direct control.
characters.name: Guppy

characters.description: A Brazilian military replicant commanding the Serra do Mar. He arrives in Epsilon Eridani earlier than Bob expects, refuses an attempt at peaceful communication, and immediately turns the encounter into a battle between competing probes.
characters.name: Major Ernesto Medeiros

characters.description: One of the first four replicants made from Bob's backup. After choosing his own name, he takes responsibility for returning toward Sol to learn what happened to humanity, and plans to create a companion for that mission.
characters.name: Riker

characters.description: One of Bob's first new replicants. He remains in Epsilon Eridani to manage production, investigate subspace communication, and begin studying the marginal world he calls Ragnarok while the other copies depart on separate missions.
characters.name: Bill

characters.description: A newly activated copy of Bob who quickly demonstrates an independent outlook. He refuses to accompany Riker to Sol and instead chooses exploration on his own terms, sharpening the early differences within the new replicant group.
characters.name: Milo

characters.description: The most reserved member of Bob's first cohort of copies. He chooses a separate identity and prepares to leave Epsilon Eridani as an independent explorer while the new replicants divide their responsibilities and destinations.
characters.name: Mario

characters.description: A replicant created from Riker's backup to share the journey to Sol. He accompanies Riker and an automated decoy vessel on a mission to investigate Earth, giving the reconnaissance team a second replicant operator.
characters.name: Homer

characters.description: Bill's newly activated copy and research partner in Epsilon Eridani. He stays behind to work on exploration drones, virtual environments, subspace physics, and artificial muscle while other replicants travel outward.
characters.name: Garfield

characters.description: A new Bob-derived replicant sent toward Alpha Centauri in a heavily upgraded Version III vessel. He travels with Goku despite their persistent friction, with both prepared for the strong possibility of encountering hostile probes.
characters.name: Calvin

characters.description: A combat-capable replicant assigned to Alpha Centauri alongside Calvin. The pair often antagonize each other but continue to cooperate, taking improved weapons, sensors, and stealth capability into a likely contested system.
characters.name: Goku

characters.description: One of three new replicants launched from Epsilon Eridani in Version III ships. Unlike Calvin and Goku, who remain paired for their mission, Linus departs separately to pursue an exploratory course of his own.
characters.name: Linus

characters.description: A Brazilian military replicant commanding one of the last probes driving asteroids toward Earth. He confronts Riker during the final stage of the Sol battle while the Bobs attempt to stop the remaining impactors.
characters.name: Captain Matthias Araujo

characters.description: Commander of a concealed United States of Eurasia refugee installation. He answers Riker's contact, reports the scale of Earth's surviving population, and presents retained colony-ship plans as the basis for an off-world rescue.
characters.name: Colonel George Butterworth

characters.description: A newly activated replicant core who joins Bob's close observation of the intelligent inhabitants of Eden. He becomes part of the small team studying their speech, behavior, and prospects while avoiding direct contact.
characters.name: Marvin

characters.description: One of the disembodied replicant cores Bob creates to expand the study of Eden's native population. Luke joins the observation project as the team works to understand the Deltans without openly revealing its presence.
characters.name: Luke

characters.description: A replicant activated with Marvin and Luke to assist Bob on Eden. He adds another independent observer to the effort to catalogue the Deltans' language, social organization, and developing technology.
characters.name: Bender

characters.description: A young Deltan distinguished by experimentation and solitary investigation. Bob gives him this name after observing him create a stone tool with a handle, an innovation that marks him as an unusual figure among his people.
characters.name: Archimedes

characters.description: A Sol-based replicant assigned to contact scattered survivor communities after the asteroid crisis. His outreach work proceeds despite deep suspicion of the Bobs, including drones being fired upon and communication devices being destroyed.
characters.name: Arthur

characters.description: A replicant who joins Riker, Homer, and Arthur in the Sol recovery effort. He helps divide the growing workload between industrial salvage, surveys of Earth, and the difficult task of locating and supporting survivor groups.
characters.name: Charles

characters.description: The negotiator for the Faith Enclave at the survivor conference. The minister argues that Faith's role in creating Riker entitles the enclave to evacuation priority, a claim Riker refuses to accept.
characters.name: Faith minister

characters.description: Representative of a small Arctic refuge whose position is becoming untenable. The leader controls access to the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults and makes that access conditional on receiving an early place in the evacuation.
characters.name: Spitsbergen leader

characters.description: An elderly Deltan who still knows the techniques of flint working. He teaches Archimedes how to shape the supplied stone and agrees to help turn the remaining material into spear points in exchange for a share of future hunts.
characters.name: Moses

characters.description: A large and influential Deltan who visibly supports Archimedes during a dispute over the new spear points. His backing helps the young toolmaker preserve the agreement that will improve the tribe's weapons.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: A living descendant of Riker's sister and therefore part of the original Bob's family line. The Faith minister presents her during evacuation negotiations to influence Riker, who begins a personal conversation without yielding on priority.
characters.name: Julia Hendricks

characters.description: An Australian replicant and former solo sailor whom Linus discovers in Epsilon Indi. Extreme isolation has left him psychotic and fused into a makeshift structure, forcing Linus to disable his reactor control before attempting a rescue.
characters.name: Henry Roberts

characters.description: A member of Calvin's first cohort who reports on the action at Alpha Centauri. With no colonizable world found and one Brazilian probe still missing, he assumes responsibility for the Bob factory established in the system.
characters.name: Bart

characters.description: A Deltan woman to whom Archimedes has become attached during the tribe's migration. Her relationship with him is evident as he takes on greater responsibilities within the group and works with Bob's guidance.
characters.name: Diana

characters.description: The replicant escort assigned to Exodus 1 and Exodus 2. His matrix is installed shortly before departure to reduce the opportunity for sabotage, and he accompanies the colonists on humanity's first interstellar evacuation voyage.
characters.name: Howard

characters.description: One of eight Version III replicants sent covertly into 82 Eridani to investigate the defenses that killed Milo and retaliate against the Brazilian presence. He enters a system protected by hidden nuclear weapons and autonomous forces.
characters.name: Khan

characters.description: One of the eight Version III replicants in the covert assault on 82 Eridani. A cloaked nuclear bomb destroys him during the approach.
characters.name: Hannibal

characters.description: A Version III replicant participating in the coordinated assault on 82 Eridani. He is part of a badly reduced force confronting cloaked bombs, numerous autonomous defenders, and the concealed Brazilian command vessel.
characters.name: Elmer

recaps.ending:
Bob and Marvin remain on Eden after helping the Deltans reach a defensible settlement. Their intervention is now overt, the tribe is better armed against gorilloids, and some Deltans have begun treating the Bobs' machines as sacred. Bill and Garfield continue Scut coordination and the long effort to add water to Ragnarok. Riker and Homer maintain the evacuation and orbital food programs in Sol.

Howard safely reaches Omicron with Exodus 1 and Exodus 2. Colonel Butterworth chooses the world with the richer ecosystem, automated equipment begins printing the settlement, and the first civilians are due to wake and descend. Exodus 3 will carry Spitsbergen, the Faith Enclave, and Riker's surviving relatives, while later ships remain necessary for millions still on Earth.

Arthur and Milo cannot be safely restored. Khan is the only physical survivor of the 82 Eridani assault and preserves his backup for another campaign because hostile autonomous units and cloaking remain. An escaped Brazilian probe is also unaccounted for. Mario must still deliver his evidence that an alien machine civilization sterilized and stripped Beta Hydri, leaving a separate threat unknown to the wider network.
recaps.in_short: After arranging cryonic preservation and dying, Bob awakens in 2133 as a software copy owned by a theocracy. Chosen to control Heaven One, a self-replicating interstellar probe, he escapes sabotage, removes his imposed controls, and begins creating independent copies. The growing replicant network explores nearby systems, fights hostile Brazilian probes, and discovers both intelligent Deltans on Eden and two habitable worlds in Omicron. Riker and Homer save a devastated Earth from a final asteroid attack, then build colony ships and orbital farms for its survivors. Bob and Marvin openly protect the Deltans and guide their migration. Arthur and Milo die without restorable backups. Mario finds evidence that an alien machine force sterilized and mined Beta Hydri, while Khan alone survives a costly attack on the Brazilian position at 82 Eridani. At the close, Howard brings Exodus 1 and Exodus 2 to Omicron, where Colonel Butterworth selects the first colony world and settlement construction begins.

recaps.text:
Bob sells his software company, arranges for cryonic preservation, and dies in a traffic accident. He next becomes aware in 2133 through electronic sensors. Dr. Landers explains that the preserved brain was destructively scanned and that this Bob is a software replication owned by a theocratic state. Bob retains his memories and identity, but his emotional responses are artificially limited.

Five replicants have been placed in competition for one assignment, with failure carrying the risk of storage, reconditioning, or destruction. Bob rapidly learns to operate cameras, remote arms, and teams of robotic roamers. He also discovers that the regime blocks access to his descendants and punishes unacceptable beliefs, so he conceals his lack of faith and concentrates on appearing useful. Several competitors are eliminated through breakdown or political judgment. After Bob successfully manages a simulated orbital station, Landers finally reveals the intended role: the remaining candidate will control a self-replicating interstellar probe. Bob and one rival are still in contention.

Project Heaven has been reduced to a single vessel and faces sabotage from factions that oppose replicants and space expansion. A raid confirms the danger, and a later bombing destroys the active replicant matrices. Bob is restored from backup into the last spare. His surviving rival is lost, leaving Bob as the only candidate able to fly the probe.

Dr. Landers grants Bob continuous awareness and, after another attack, secretly gives him operating-system access. Bob is installed aboard Heaven One, a converted freighter bound for Epsilon Eridani. Missiles arrive before the planned launch, forcing him to break away early and destroy his pursuer. The orbital station is destroyed behind him.

Once in flight, Bob removes a concealed explosive device, software imperatives requiring obedience, and traps intended to accept a remote kill command. He constructs a detailed virtual environment to manage isolation and begins planning for defense and replication. Messages identify the attacker as a Brazilian gunship, warn of another probe on his course, and report that Landers has been killed. As Bob finally allows himself to grieve, observations of Earth indicate that nuclear detonations are occurring on the surface.

Bob reaches Epsilon Eridani, mines its asteroid belt, and prepares for the pursuing Brazilian probe. Major Ernesto Medeiros arrives aboard the Serra do Mar, rejects communication, and attacks. Bob's automated weapons destroy the hostile vessel, though Heaven One takes repairable damage. Expecting further enemies, Bob decides that future ships must be armed.

The system offers resources but no obvious colony world. Bob overcomes his discomfort about duplication and constructs four new replicants and upgraded vessels. The copies choose the names Riker, Bill, Milo, and Mario, and their personalities immediately begin to diverge. Bill remains in Epsilon Eridani to manage production, communications research, and investigation of Ragnarok. Riker plans to return to Sol with a copy of his own. Bob leaves for Delta Eridani, Milo chooses Omicron, and Mario heads toward Beta Hydri.

At Omicron, Milo discovers a paired set of living worlds, which he names Vulcan and Romulus. Both have oceans, oxygenated atmospheres, green land, and apparently related ecosystems. Heavy elements are scarce locally, but Milo begins refining material from a Jovian planet's moons and testing whether the native biology could support human settlers.

Riker and his copy Homer travel toward Sol, while Bill's copy Garfield becomes his partner in Epsilon Eridani research. Riker's covert survey finds a nuclear-ravaged Earth and at least six Brazilian probes preparing to drive four large bodies into the planet. Bill also launches Calvin, Goku, and Linus in stronger Version III ships as the replicant network expands.

Riker and Homer lure four attackers away and destroy them. During the final engagement Homer is disabled, but his core survives. Riker destroys the last Brazilian vessels, including the one commanded by Captain Matthias Araujo, then takes control of the asteroid drives and diverts all four impactors. Earth has escaped this final attack, although earlier war and strikes have already caused immense damage.

Bill and Garfield prove that subspace signals avoid ordinary light-speed delay and design a relay-based communications system. In Sol, Colonel George Butterworth contacts Riker from an underground refugee installation holding about 20,000 people. Fewer than 20 million humans may remain worldwide. Earth is not expected to recover fast enough, but the refugees possess colony-ship plans. They ask the Bobs to build the ships and find a viable destination, turning the Sol mission into an interstellar evacuation project.

Bob reaches Delta Eridani and discovers an intelligent, fire-using native species on a living world later called Eden. He begins covert observation and names the people Deltans. An inventive youth, Archimedes, attracts his attention by creating a handled stone tool. Marvin, Luke, and Bender join the study as additional replicants.

Elsewhere, Calvin and Goku attack a Brazilian manufacturing yard at Alpha Centauri. They destroy most of the installation and its defenders, but one incomplete vessel escapes and another probe may already have departed. In Sol, Riker, Homer, Charles, and Arthur expand salvage and contact nearly forty survivor communities. Material is sufficient for only a few colony ships, while the population is about fifteen million. Political conflict grows over evacuation order, especially when the Spitsbergen refuge makes access to the Svalbard vaults conditional on priority and a Faith minister claims ownership of Riker.

Milo's report confirms Omicron as a possible destination. On Eden, repeated gorilloid attacks show that the Deltans have long been hunted and displaced. Bob's group decides that noninterference could mean extinction. They covertly supply flint, enabling Archimedes and the elder Moses to improve the tribe's axes and spears. Arnold supports the new weapons, and the Deltans successfully repel another attack.

The Earth survivor groups remain divided, but a compromise emerges: Spitsbergen can receive the third colony ship in exchange for access to the Svalbard vaults. The Faith minister tries to invoke an old control protocol against Riker, only to learn that Bob removed it. The minister later introduces Julia Hendricks, a descendant of Riker's sister, as leverage. Riker speaks with her but does not change the allocation rules.

A major gorilloid assault kills more than forty Deltans. Bob exposes his intervention by directly using a defensive drone to save Archimedes. He and Marvin conclude that the tribe should migrate to an older settlement with flint, water, and better defenses. Luke and Bender leave for separate missions, while Bob and Marvin prepare to speak to the Deltans openly.

At Epsilon Indi, Linus finds Henry Roberts, an Australian replicant driven psychotic by prolonged sensory deprivation. Linus disables and retrieves him, then places him in a sailing simulation based on his former life, where Henry becomes lucid. Bill's subspace system, Scut, reconnects the distant Bobs without perceptible delay. Riker can now present Omicron's two living worlds as confirmed destinations, although Earth's survivor groups object to sharing them.

Two colony ships near completion, but limited material and Earth's worsening climate make it impossible to save everyone quickly. Bob openly contacts Archimedes through a speaking drone and asks him to persuade the Deltans to move. The elders debate the proposal. Bart reports that Alpha Centauri remains under Bob control, although a Brazilian probe escaped and has not been found.

Milo begins surveying two possible colony worlds in 82 Eridani, then is ambushed by eight missiles. He transmits a report and partial backup while expecting his ship to be destroyed. In Sol, sabotage worsens the food crisis. Arthur is killed by a nuclear trap during salvage near Saturn, and because no off-ship backup exists, he cannot be restored. Riker and Homer plan better backup storage as well as a memorial.

The Deltans finally begin their migration after Bob teaches them to preserve meat. A gorilloid raid kills a juvenile, prompting Bob and Marvin to locate smaller Deltan bands and bring them into the group. More than 500 migrants cross the mountain pass and reach the forest with supplies remaining, but they have entered unfamiliar territory where daytime predator attacks are difficult to prevent.

Homer proposes rotating orbital farms to answer Earth's starvation threat, and Riker approves the plan. The Faith Enclave trades food reserves for likely passage on the third colony ship. Farm One begins delivering crops, and the next farm should provide a temporary surplus, though Earthside production continues to decline.

Milo's final transmission confirms that his vessel was destroyed at 82 Eridani. His partial backup is unsafe to restore, so Bill records his death and prepares eight armed replicants for retaliation. Bob and Marvin survive another mass gorilloid raid, replenish their defenses, and lead the Deltans to the former flint site. The new settlement has water, visibility, and strong natural defenses. Bob tries to condition local gorilloids to avoid it, while some Deltans begin treating pieces of his machines as sacred objects.

The first two Exodus ships are completed. Bill and Garfield also deliver an iceberg to Ragnarok as rain, though the operation destroys important drive hardware. At Beta Hydri, Mario finds missing metals, a wreck full of refined ingots, mechanical devices that attack his roamer, and evidence of a system sterilized by radiation decades earlier. He infers that a machine force mined the system, but cannot yet report the discovery to the network.

Exodus 1 and Exodus 2 load colonists and seed-vault material, then leave Earth under Howard's protection. Exodus 3, assigned to Spitsbergen, the Faith Enclave, and Riker's surviving relatives, is due to follow, with additional ships under construction. Bill hosts the first network-wide gathering of the increasingly varied replicant community.

Eight Version III replicants attack the Brazilian position at 82 Eridani. Cloaked nuclear weapons and autonomous defenders destroy most of the force. The attackers apparently eliminate the Brazilian replicant, but only Khan escapes physically; Elmer sacrifices himself to maintain the jamming that makes Khan's survival possible. Hostile machines and cloaking technology remain, so Khan saves his backup for a future return. The escaped Alpha Centauri probe is also still missing.

Howard reaches Omicron with the first two colony ships. Automated equipment has accumulated materials and started backup food production. Colonel Butterworth selects the more biologically rich of the two candidate worlds, and construction crews begin printing homes and infrastructure before the civilians wake. Humanity's first settlement beyond Earth is therefore beginning. Bob and Marvin remain with the Deltans, Bill and Garfield continue their research and terraforming work, and Riker and Homer continue supporting the evacuation and Earth's food supply. Arthur and Milo remain permanently lost, while Mario's evidence of a separate alien machine threat has not yet reached the others.

characters.description: The eighteen-year-old narrator, who lives in near-total isolation with her sister Constance and their uncle Julian. Merricat is intensely protective of the household, devoted to private rituals, and openly hostile toward the villagers who torment her. She makes the weekly trip into town for supplies and otherwise prefers the grounds of the family estate, accompanied by her cat Jonas.
characters.name: Mary Katherine Blackwood

characters.description: Merricat's older sister and the practical center of the surviving Blackwood household. Constance cooks, gardens, and gently cares for Uncle Julian, but has not gone beyond the garden since she was tried and acquitted after the rest of the family died. Her warmth and domestic confidence contrast with her fear of the outside world.
characters.name: Constance Blackwood

characters.description: The elderly surviving Blackwood uncle, physically disabled and absorbed in reconstructing the family catastrophe. Julian repeatedly reviews the meal, the deaths, and the investigation in his notes, often treating Merricat as though she were no longer alive. Constance patiently tends him.
characters.name: Julian Blackwood

characters.description: Merricat's black cat and constant companion outdoors. Jonas follows her through the Blackwood grounds and belongs to the private, almost enchanted order she imagines around the estate.
characters.name: Jonas

characters.description: The owner of the village café where Merricat pauses during her supply trips. Stella speaks to her with more ordinary kindness than most villagers do, though her efforts do not shield Merricat from the cruelty of other customers.
characters.name: Stella

characters.description: A village man who needles Merricat in Stella's café and joins the familiar public harassment directed at the Blackwoods. His mock friendliness makes the villagers' hostility especially clear.
characters.name: Jim Donell

characters.description: A local woman who keeps visiting Constance despite the Blackwoods' withdrawal from village society. Helen is energetic, inquisitive, and determined to draw Constance back into ordinary social life, a project Merricat regards as an intrusion.
characters.name: Helen Clarke

characters.description: Helen Clarke's husband, who accompanies her to tea at the Blackwood house. His questions encourage Uncle Julian to recount the family's history and create an awkward collision between the household's private routines and outside curiosity.
characters.name: Jim Clarke

characters.description: A Blackwood cousin who arrives after years away and presents himself as a friendly relative. Charming and attentive toward Constance, he quickly takes an interest in the household's money and authority. Merricat distrusts him from the start and sees his growing influence as a threat to the sisters' closed world.
characters.name: Charles Blackwood

characters.description: The late head of the Blackwood household, remembered as strict, controlling, and possessive about money. His presence survives in the house's rules and objects, especially the safe and the dining room where the family gathered.
characters.name: John Blackwood

characters.description: Merricat and Constance's younger brother, one of the family members who died at the Blackwood dinner. Uncle Julian's attempts to recreate that evening repeatedly return to the child's place at the table.
characters.name: Thomas Blackwood

characters.description: Uncle Julian's late wife, who lived with the Blackwoods and died with most of the family. She appears through Julian's fragmented, obsessive account of the fatal meal and the household tensions surrounding it.
characters.name: Dorothy Blackwood

recaps.ending: After the fire and the villagers' destruction of the house, Constance and Merricat wall themselves off in the surviving kitchen and a few adjoining rooms. Uncle Julian has died, Charles has abandoned his attempt to control Constance and the family money, and the sisters refuse invitations or official help. Ashamed villagers begin leaving food at the door, while local children turn the ruined Blackwood place into a source of fearful stories. Merricat admits to Constance that she put arsenic in the sugar because she knew Constance never used it; Constance already knows and responds without breaking their bond. The sisters settle into an even smaller and more secluded version of their old life. Hidden from view, supplied by offerings, and answerable only to each other, they regard their isolation as happiness rather than rescue or punishment.
recaps.in_short: Eighteen-year-old Merricat Blackwood lives with her agoraphobic sister Constance and invalid Uncle Julian after arsenic in the sugar killed the rest of their wealthy family. Constance was acquitted of the murders, but the village still treats the sisters with suspicion and cruelty. Their sealed domestic life is disturbed when cousin Charles arrives, courts Constance's trust, and tries to impose authority on the house. Merricat's efforts to drive him away lead to a fire. Villagers who come to watch and supposedly help instead wreck the home, and Julian dies. Constance and Merricat retreat into the surviving rooms. Merricat, not Constance, poisoned the family, a truth Constance accepts. As ashamed neighbors leave food outside and legends grow around the ruined estate, the sisters embrace permanent isolation together.

recaps.text: Mary Katherine Blackwood, called Merricat, makes her regular trip from the family estate into a village that openly despises her. Six years earlier, arsenic in the sugar bowl killed most of the Blackwood family. Merricat's older sister Constance was tried and acquitted, yet remains the object of local suspicion and has not left the grounds since. The only other survivor at home is their disabled Uncle Julian, who compulsively studies the deaths while Constance cares for him. Merricat experiences the village's taunts as an assault and protects herself with private rules and magical rituals. Back at the estate, she feels secure with Constance, Julian, and her cat Jonas, and wishes their enclosed household could remain unchanged.

The Blackwoods' carefully contained routine is interrupted by Helen and Jim Clarke, who come to tea. Helen wants Constance to rejoin village society, while Jim's interest in the old crime prompts Uncle Julian to reconstruct the fatal dinner in unsettling detail. Constance handles the visit graciously, but Merricat resents the outsiders and tries to restore the house to its familiar order after they leave. Julian's memories establish how completely the family tragedy controls the survivors' present: for him it is an endless investigation, for Constance a reason to remain home, and for Merricat a boundary separating their safe world from everyone beyond it.

Cousin Charles Blackwood arrives and quickly wins Constance's attention by behaving like a practical, affectionate relative. He dismisses Uncle Julian's confused hostility and treats Merricat as a badly behaved child. His interest in the family's safe, money, and valuable possessions makes Merricat certain he has come to take control. Constance begins considering changes Charles encourages, including a less isolated life, while Merricat's warnings fail to move her. Merricat tries spells, insults, and small acts of disruption to force him out, but Charles becomes increasingly established in her father's room and at the family table. The stable alliance between the sisters begins to strain under his presence.

Merricat's conflict with Charles culminates when she puts his smoking pipe into a wastebasket in the room he has claimed. The house catches fire. Constance gets Uncle Julian outside, but Charles is preoccupied with rescuing the safe, and Julian is taken away in serious condition. Villagers gather as firefighters contain the blaze. Once the danger has passed, the crowd turns on the Blackwood home, smashing furniture, dishes, windows, and food with the enthusiasm of a long-awaited punishment. Merricat and Constance flee into the woods while Charles leaves with what property he can carry. Hidden in Merricat's woodland refuge, the sisters hear the destruction of the life they knew.

Merricat and Constance return after the crowd has gone. Much of the upper house is burned and the rooms below have been deliberately wrecked, but the kitchen and a small portion of the building remain usable. They learn that Uncle Julian has died. Rather than go to friends or accept a new public life, the sisters clean the surviving space, block sightlines from outside, and plan how to live unseen. Constance is shaken by guilt over fleeing and by the loss of Julian, yet her bond with Merricat holds. Charles comes back and calls for Constance, but the sisters stay silent until he leaves. Their response to catastrophe is to make the household smaller, more secret, and harder for outsiders to enter.

Constance and Merricat establish a new life inside the ruined house, using only the surviving rooms and moving where no passerby can see them. Shame replaces some of the village's open aggression: people leave baskets of food at the door, sometimes with apologetic notes, while rumors and children's stories turn the sisters into legendary figures. Helen Clarke asks them to return to society, but they refuse every approach. Merricat confirms to Constance that she poisoned the family's sugar because Constance did not take sugar and would therefore survive; Constance has already understood. No confession, arrest, or reconciliation follows. With Julian dead and Charles gone, the sisters accept a permanent shared seclusion. The feared house becomes both their refuge and their whole world, and they declare themselves happy there.

characters.description: A homeless recent graduate on Earth whose parents died in a truck collision. Unable to afford college, Chance tries to live by the optimism and contentment they taught him, showing generosity even when he has almost nothing before a truck strikes and kills him.
characters.name: Chance

characters.description: A truck driver who tests Chance's generosity, displays surprising strength, and asks whether he would accept a new life with genuine agency. After abruptly disappearing from their conversation, he deliberately drives the semi-truck that strikes and kills Chance.
characters.name: The trucker

characters.description: An extraordinarily powerful floating man who heals Chance after his ordeal in the alleys and opens a path to safety. He claims a connection through their essence, treats Chance as an investment, and demands absolute secrecy under threat of death.
characters.name: The floating man

characters.description: A grey-haired trainer whom Chance first sees defeating an armored trainee during a spar. He is present when Chance finally emerges from the lethal alleys onto a monster-hunter training field and collapses after asking for food and water.
characters.name: The grey-haired trainer

characters.description: The resident instructor and supervisor for Chance's new team. Pete provides a home, explains the risks and rewards of monster hunting, and supports the recruits' development while keeping some of the head trainer's history private.
characters.name: Pete

characters.description: A capable and independently productive hunter who had an agreement to work alone until she was assigned to Chance's team. Bella blames the unexpected change on his arrival, rejects him outright, and refuses to accept the imposed team arrangement.
characters.name: Bella

characters.description: Chance's enthusiastic third teammate, a Kusarigama user from a nearby village whose father came from Earth. Curious about Chance's home world, he quickly proposes an exchange of knowledge and becomes Chance's cooperative early ally.
characters.name: The metal cultivator teammate

characters.description: A weapon specialist who reads affinity through essence. When conventional armory choices fail Chance, the battlemaster follows the pull of Chance's power to a dangerous segmented blade and begins identifying the weapon suited to him.
characters.name: Battlemaster Jag

characters.description: A powerful figure who reaches Bella through an isolating ward and holds her to a binding contract. Vex calls her an investment, immobilizes Chance when he witnesses their meeting, and is prepared to kill him before another cultivator intervenes.
characters.name: Vex

characters.description: The shifting old alleys that secretly draw Chance into real hunts and reward him with monster corpses. Their routes and gifts respond to him in purposeful ways, but the nature of the force directing these encounters remains unexplained.
characters.name: The Old City alleys

characters.description: A recruit from the metal cultivator teammate's hometown who arrives with another new team. Their existing rivalry is immediately apparent, and his presence establishes a personal contest that the teammate is unwilling to explain to Chance.
characters.name: The hometown rival

characters.description: A powerful hunter who takes charge when the team's imp investigation exceeds foundling level. Joe uses a ring to form a fast-flying metal disc and brings the recruits along to search for the missing mother rather than letting them continue alone.
characters.name: Joe

characters.description: The newly conscious part of Gleam that has been communicating through altered passages and stone images. The Old City says it gathers stray essence to cultivate, opposes the cultivator who enslaves people through karma, and asks Chance for a provisional alliance.
characters.name: The Old City

characters.description: The hidden nature of the floating man Chance has known since the alleys. He is an essence clone of a vastly stronger karma cultivator, and his path uses karmic enslavement to create transformed monsters. The Old City warns that he will eventually report Chance to his true self.
characters.name: The senior karma cultivator's essence clone

characters.description: An immortal karma cultivator drawn to Chance by the appearance of a new practitioner. Lucy warns that karmic power carries mounting costs and offers timeless mindscape instruction in exchange for a favor that Chance must repay in the future.
characters.name: Lucy

characters.description: The armored tournament opponent revealed to be the metal cultivator teammate's brother. He makes their match a public dispute over their father, claiming the family rejected his brother while favoring him, but loses after his brother endures grave injuries and traps him with metal threads.
characters.name: The metal cultivator teammate's brother

characters.description: A tournament fighter whose polearm movements are inseparable from his essence of endless dance. His integrated style exposes what Chance's own method lacks, and he initially uses their match as an opportunity to guide Chance rather than simply defeat him.
characters.name: The polearm dancer

characters.description: The polearm dancer's plainly dressed but immensely powerful teacher. He interrupts the tournament after his student uses a prohibited technique, exerting enough pressure to nearly crush both Chance and the dancer before forcing his student to withdraw.
characters.name: The polearm dancer's mentor

characters.description: The true cultivator behind the essence clone who has shaped Chance's progress. After taking direct control of the fragment, he reveals his interest in controlling the awakened Old City and offers Chance a marked apprenticeship tied to an agreement over its fate.
characters.name: The senior karma cultivator

recaps.ending: Chance is bound to the awakened Old City and marked as the senior karma cultivator's apprentice, although he has openly rejected the cultivator's plan to control it. After the order sends an assassin for Bella, Chance saves her and Pete covers their escape. Chance and Bella use the Old City's passages and unrecorded transit tokens to leave Gleam, then enter a forest as supplied but vulnerable fugitives. Their metal cultivator teammate survives a separate attack, kills his assassin with a concealed blade, and disappears inside Gleam. Pete remains behind, and his later situation is unknown. Vex still intends to kill Bella for the life debt he claims, though negotiations with the senior cultivator have delayed a direct confrontation. Lucy and her mentor continue to watch. The Old City is Chance's ally but remains imprisoned by five transformed-monster seals. Chance has not found his parents, cannot yet afford the uncertain search, and still owes Lucy a future favor.
recaps.in_short: After dying on Earth, Chance awakens in Gleam, joins a three-person monster-hunting team, and discovers that his apparent luck is karma essence. His secret guide trains him while cultivating him for its own purposes, and Chance later learns that the guide is a clone whose karmic enslavement turns people into monsters. He allies with the awakened Old City against that clone, advances to Squire, develops a personal Urumi style, and wins a major tournament. Bella abandons Vex's borrowed methods for preservation cultivation, while their metal cultivator teammate becomes Chance's friendly rival. The true senior karma cultivator eventually takes Chance as a marked apprentice and has the Old City bind itself to him. When the order moves against the team, Chance saves Bella from an assassin and flees Gleam with her. Their teammate escapes a separate killer inside the city, Pete stays behind, Vex's lethal claim on Bella remains active, and Chance's parents remain unfound.

recaps.text: Chance, a homeless graduate on Earth, returns a trucker's wallet and pays for the stranger's drinks. The trucker questions whether Chance would accept a life with genuine choice, then deliberately kills him with a semi-truck. Chance awakens in unfamiliar stone alleys beneath a purple sky. A note from the trucker hints that Chance's dead parents may also be in this world. After eating the food left with the note, Chance purges black bile and manifests golden mist that bends events in his favor. He survives for weeks among monstrous hounds before a floating man heals him, claims an unspecified connection through their essence, and orders him to keep their meeting secret. Chance escapes to a training field in Gleam, where the head trainer registers him as a monster hunter and assigns him to a team. Pete becomes his resident instructor, while Bella resents being forced out of solo work. When the head trainer plans to report Chance's abnormal arrival, the floating man threatens his wife and compels him to support Chance instead.

Team Whiteheart gains its third recruit, a friendly metal cultivator whose father came from Earth and who fights with a Kusarigama. He and Chance agree to pursue rank and money together, partly to fund a search for Chance's parents, while Bella continues to avoid them. Chance learns the basics of essence, aura, cultivation, and the hunter ranking system. Pete finds that Chance's golden mist can redirect an attack, and a battlemaster identifies the dangerous Urumi as Chance's natural weapon. During secret visits to the Old City, Chance receives combat training and monster corpses from the floating cultivator. Bella's isolation acquires a clearer cause when Vex reaches her inside a ward, invokes a binding contract, and calls her his investment. Vex immobilizes Chance and prepares to kill him for witnessing their meeting. The floating cultivator intervenes, destroys Vex's remote manifestation, and declares Chance under his protection. Bella then asks Chance to leave with her so she can explain the danger.

Bella explains that association with Vex endangers anyone close to her, but an oath prevents a full account. Chance and the metal cultivator teammate refuse to abandon her, turning the imposed group into a willing team. Chance identifies his essence as karma, with luck as one expression of it. The Old City cultivator confirms the same path and secures a temporary noninterference agreement from Vex, though he also says he is raising Chance for a future harvest. Bella teaches cultivation while the teammate teaches combat, and Chance gradually controls the Urumi. The three pass their team examination and become foundling hunters. Individual ranking matches expose their weaknesses: Bella is advanced but relies on borrowed forms, the teammate fights too independently, and Chance lacks a safe way to combine essence with his weapon. Chance is disqualified after attempting that combination without a technique pattern. Bella withdraws voluntarily, while the teammate reaches the final but loses to a stronger armored metal cultivator. The team completes the assessment qualified for paid hunting, but Chance receives no individual placement.

The team receives wards, collection orbs, and funds for its first jobs. In the Old City, Chance survives a stronger suit hound by forming a golden third eye that reveals karmic strands. He learns to claim a strand to manifest its associated force or sever it for a temporary advantage, but rejects the cultivator's demand that he avoid all personal debts. Bella abandons Vex-linked water forms and begins creating black ice as her own method. On their first shared assignment, the team investigates reports of a lesser imp and finds evidence that the apparent victim's mother has been replaced by a greater imp. Chance's karmic sight exposes the disguised creature in magical darkness, allowing Bella and the teammate to defeat it. They rescue the sleeping boy, and the stronger hunter Joe finds his real mother alive and transfers the wider threat to experienced hunters. Elsewhere, a night-ranked hunter becomes trapped in the Old City. After hundreds of hounds exhaust him, Chance's secret cultivator declares him payment for debts incurred there and destroys him, confirming that the city's hidden danger extends far beyond Chance's lessons.

Bella and the metal cultivator teammate advance to Squire before Chance. The Old City forces Chance into a severe trial that ends in a vision of a golden eight-armed being, and he completes his own advancement soon afterward. A specialist could search Centurion for Chance's parents, but the estimated cost is about seventeen thousand gold with no guarantee of success. Chance continues private hunts and learns that some suit hounds and imps are transformed humans. He has already killed and eaten one such victim, and he resolves to seek a way to save others. During a public job, the Old City draws Bella and the teammate into its shifting alleys and deposits extra monster corpses for the team. Chance confronts it for risking his friends and defeats a chained transformed hound before demanding the truth. The Old City reveals itself as a newly awakened portion of Gleam. It says Chance's guide is an essence clone whose karma path enslaves people and creates the transformed monsters. Five such creatures help bind the city. Chance accepts only a provisional alliance against the clone and promises to keep the city's awareness secret.

The Old City gives Chance a stronger Urumi that can fold into a bracelet, in exchange for help against the essence clone and a promise not to exploit the city. Bella explains that she removed the last of Vex's essence-infused water from herself, sacrificing stored power to escape his control. The clone sends a karmic signal toward its distant true self. Chance, Bella, and their teammate continue hunting and training for the quarterly Squire tournament, while Chance uses cultivation pills without the impurity limits that constrain the others. Lucy, an immortal karma cultivator, discovers Chance and offers timeless mindscape instruction for a future favor. Her training gives him a foundation of balance, redirection, and fluid movement, but he must adapt it into a style that embodies his own essence. Lucy then traces Chance's connection to the clone. She and her mentor choose to observe unless the senior cultivator clearly intends to kill him. With the larger danger approaching and tournament rewards offering money and resources, Chance and both teammates enter the Squire competition.

All three teammates progress deep into the Squire tournament. The metal cultivator teammate defeats an armored opponent revealed as his brother, surviving terrible wounds by stitching himself together with metal threads. The brother publicly exposes a family grievance involving their father's rejection and favoritism. Bella loses to a polearm dancer whose endless-dance essence is fully integrated with his fighting style. Watching him helps Chance understand what his borrowed movements lack. In their match, Chance stops forcing his power and finds a joyful style built on karma, luck, and faith in a favorable outcome. The dancer uses a prohibited technique, prompting his mentor to intervene, and withdraws from the event. Chance reaches the final against his own teammate. They declare themselves friendly public rivals and fight until Chance places his Urumi at the teammate's neck while trapped in a field of metal threads. The teammate concedes, making Chance the tournament winner. The victory brings both finalists recognition and leaves the teammate determined to challenge Chance again after learning aura.

Chance directs the polearm dancer's offered compensation toward instruction for Bella's preservation essence. Vex enters Gleam to collect the life debt he claims from Bella, and the senior karma cultivator restrains him long enough to negotiate. Vex states plainly that repayment means killing Bella and recovering the power he invested in her. The senior cultivator insists that she receive a fighting chance but suggests their wider goals may align. After the dancer warns Chance that powerful figures are watching the team, Chance is drawn into the Old City. The true senior cultivator takes control of his clone, demonstrates overwhelming power, and admits wanting the awakened city's strength. Chance opposes enslaving it, yet accepts a marked apprenticeship when the cultivator agrees that the city may bind itself to Chance and eventually go free. His first compulsory task is to prevent Bella's death and the team's detention. Guided by the city, Chance intercepts an assassin attacking Bella through her window. He incapacitates the attacker, and Pete returns in time to cover Chance and Bella as they flee their home and become fugitives from the order.

Chance brings Bella through the Old City's concealed routes toward Gleam's edge. He finally tells her that he died on Earth, survived for weeks in the alleys, and has been dealing with the senior karma cultivator and the awakened city. Bella learns that Chance's body has no impurities, apologizes for treating him as an outsider, and promises to protect the city's secret. Elsewhere, the metal cultivator teammate receives a warning that the order is sending killers after all three recruits. An assassin traps him in a ward, but he kills the attacker with a concealed blade that desiccates the body and disappears separately inside Gleam. Chance and Bella briefly leave the Old City to buy supplies, then use its passages to reach a main gate. They choose free transit tokens that carry no recorded named destination and arrive in fields beside a forest outside the city. They enter the forest to evade pursuit. Chance and Bella are safely beyond Gleam for the moment, but remain fugitives in uncertain territory. Their teammate is alive but separated, Pete has stayed behind, and Vex's claim on Bella, the order's pursuit, the senior cultivator's demands, and the Old City's imprisonment all remain unresolved.

characters.description: A thirty-nine-year-old Sydney mother who hits her head during a spin class and wakes believing she is twenty-nine, newly married, and pregnant with her first child. The missing decade has left her facing three children she does not remember, a changed family, and a marriage close to divorce. Her warmer younger outlook often conflicts with evidence that she had become highly driven and controlling.
characters.name: Alice Love

characters.description: Alice's husband, whom she remembers as the affectionate newlywed eagerly preparing for their first baby. In the present he is separated from her and involved in a bitter custody dispute. Alice cannot reconcile his anger with the man she believes she saw only the day before.
characters.name: Nick Love

characters.description: Alice's older sister, once her closest confidante. Elisabeth has endured repeated fertility treatment and losses with her husband Ben, while her relationship with Alice has become distant for reasons Alice cannot remember. Her written reflections provide another account of the family's difficult decade.
characters.name: Elisabeth

characters.description: Elisabeth's patient husband. He shares the strain of their long effort to become parents and tries to support her as treatment, grief, and uncertainty reshape their life together.
characters.name: Ben

characters.description: Alice and Nick's eldest child. Madison is approaching adolescence and has a tense, guarded relationship with her mother. She is old enough to understand the separation and to test whether Alice's changed behavior can be trusted.
characters.name: Madison Love

characters.description: Alice and Nick's son, one of the three children Alice has no memory of raising. His routines and loyalties reflect a family already accustomed to moving between separated parents.
characters.name: Tom Love

characters.description: Alice and Nick's youngest child. Olivia's presence makes Alice's missing decade tangible: Alice remembers expecting a first baby but is now meeting the third child of her marriage.
characters.name: Olivia Love

characters.description: Alice and Elisabeth's mother. In the decade Alice cannot remember, Barb has become energetic, socially busy, and remarried, another transformation that makes the present feel unfamiliar to Alice.
characters.name: Barb

characters.description: The school principal and Alice's present-day romantic companion. He knows the competent, separated version of Alice, not the younger-minded woman who wakes after the accident still in love with Nick.
characters.name: Dominick

characters.description: Alice's close friend from the missing decade. Gina's forceful personality and influence were woven into Alice's social life, fitness, and changing marriage. Her absence in the present is one of the painful facts Alice gradually has to understand.
characters.name: Gina

characters.description: An older family friend who writes candid letters about love, age, and loneliness. Her perspective forms a quieter counterpoint to Alice's amnesia and Elisabeth's struggle to imagine a different future.
characters.name: Frannie

recaps.ending: Alice's memories return enough for her to understand the grief, resentment, and habits that brought her marriage to the point of divorce, especially the effect of Gina's friendship and death. Remembering does not erase what happened, but the perspective of her twenty-nine-year-old self has shown her that the hostile version of family life she inherited is not inevitable. She ends her relationship with Dominik and, after confronting both the genuine injuries and the enduring affection between them, reconciles with Nick. They rebuild their marriage rather than continuing the custody battle. Alice also renews her closeness with Elisabeth and becomes more attentive to what her sister's long experience of infertility has cost. Elisabeth and Ben finally move toward parenthood and a less treatment-dominated life. The later view of the family shows Alice and Nick together, their children older, and the relationships changed by Alice's accident continuing in a more forgiving form.
recaps.in_short: After a fall at the gym, thirty-nine-year-old Alice Love loses all memory of the previous decade. She believes she is twenty-nine, happily married to Nick, and pregnant for the first time, but discovers that she has three children, is separating from Nick, and has grown distant from her sister Elisabeth. Meeting her children and the efficient, combative person she had become forces Alice to reconstruct how work, parenthood, resentment, and her intense friendship with Gina changed her marriage. Gina's death lies behind much of the grief Alice cannot initially understand. Her younger outlook disrupts the custody conflict and restores connections her older self had neglected. As her memory returns, Alice accepts the real causes of the separation without accepting that divorce is the only possible ending. She leaves her newer relationship, reconciles with Nick, repairs her bond with Elisabeth, and helps create a more forgiving future for the family.

recaps.text: Alice Love falls during a spin class and wakes disoriented, believing she is twenty-nine, newly married to Nick, and pregnant with their first child. She is actually thirty-nine and has lost ten years of memory. The people around her look older and behave with a caution she does not understand. Her sister Elisabeth, once her closest companion, seems guarded and exhausted, while her mother Barb has built a life Alice does not recognize. Nick is not immediately at her side, and the affectionate marriage Alice remembers is plainly no longer the marriage everyone else knows. Alice initially treats the gap as a temporary mistake, but each conversation reveals another major change she cannot explain.

Alice learns that she and Nick are separated and moving toward divorce. Even more startling, they have three children: Madison, Tom, and Olivia. Alice has no memories of pregnancy, birth, or years of parenting them, while the children know a stricter, busier mother than the warm newlywed she still feels herself to be. Nick speaks to her with anger rooted in conflicts she cannot remember, and their custody arrangements show how far the family has divided. Alice also discovers that she has a present-day relationship with the school principal, Dominik, though emotionally she still regards Nick as her husband. Elisabeth's distance is connected to years of fertility treatment and sorrow that Alice's younger self has not yet witnessed. The lost decade is no longer an abstract blank: it contains the formation and near-collapse of Alice's family.

Trying to resume daily life, Alice meets the children on unfamiliar terms and finds that her amnesia sometimes softens established battles. Madison remains suspicious, while the younger children reveal routines Alice is expected to know. Evidence of Alice's former schedule, fitness, school work, and social authority suggests that she became exceptionally organized but less open and affectionate. A missing figure named Gina emerges as central to those changes. Gina was Alice's closest friend during the forgotten years and strongly influenced her habits and view of Nick. Alice gradually learns that Gina died, leaving grief and unfinished anger embedded in the marriage. Meanwhile Elisabeth's account of repeated failed attempts to have a child shows how much pain Alice overlooked while absorbed in her own household and friendship.

Alice continues organizing a large school fund-raising event even though she cannot remember creating it. The project exposes both the competence of her older self and the pressure she habitually placed on others. She spends time with Nick and the children, sometimes recreating the ease of their earlier family life, but Nick cannot simply forget the resentment that accumulated over years. Dominik offers a gentler present-day relationship, yet Alice still experiences it as belonging to someone else. Fragmentary memories connect Gina's death to Alice's emotional withdrawal and to conflicts in which Nick felt displaced. Alice also begins to see that her estrangement from Elisabeth was not one dramatic quarrel but a pattern of failing to notice her sister's losses. The accident gives her a chance to behave differently before she fully remembers why these relationships broke down.

As the school event approaches, Alice's memories return in flashes, bringing back not only affection but the exhaustion, grief, and mutual blame hidden by her idealized picture of marriage. She understands more clearly how her bond with Gina, Gina's death, parenting pressures, and repeated disappointments hardened her relationship with Nick. Nick sees that the post-accident Alice is not merely pretending to change, but he remains wary of rebuilding a marriage that hurt them both. Alice pulls away from Dominik because she cannot treat him as a substitute answer while her feelings for Nick remain active. Her renewed attention to Elisabeth also forces the sisters to acknowledge the loneliness caused by infertility and by Alice's absence when Elisabeth most needed her.

Alice regains enough of the missing decade to understand why she and Nick separated, but she also retains the perspective created by forgetting it. Rather than return unchanged to the efficient, angry person she had become, she uses what she has learned from both versions of herself. She ends her relationship with Dominik and she and Nick acknowledge the injuries beneath their hostility as well as the attachment that survives. They reconcile and begin rebuilding their marriage and family life instead of continuing toward divorce. Alice repairs her closeness with Elisabeth, taking her sister's grief and hopes seriously; Elisabeth and Ben move toward becoming parents after years dominated by treatment and loss. In the later view of their lives, Alice and Nick remain together, their children have grown, and the accident's interruption of old habits has become a lasting change rather than a brief return to the past.

characters.description: A senior St Mary's historian given responsibility for a new group of trainees. Her experience makes her an effective crisis leader, but the habits that kept her alive in the field do not always translate neatly into a safe teaching programme.
characters.name: Madeleine Maxwell

characters.description: Head of Technical and Max's partner. He is responsible for the pods used by her trainees and therefore has to balance support for Max with an engineer's resistance to avoidable risks.
characters.name: Leon Farrell

characters.description: Director of St Mary's and the authority who assigns Max to training. He expects her to turn inexperienced recruits into historians without allowing the institute's enemies or its own traditions to consume them.
characters.name: Edward Bairstow

characters.description: A veteran historian and one of Max's closest colleagues. Peterson helps judge the recruits' progress and provides a steadier model of field practice when training moves into live historical settings.
characters.name: Tim Peterson

characters.description: St Mary's senior security officer. Guthrie prepares the trainees for physical danger and becomes essential when an exercise begins to show signs of a real hostile intervention.
characters.name: Ian Guthrie

characters.description: A Security operative whose unconventional competence makes him well suited to demonstrations in which plans fail and immediate action matters more than appearances.
characters.name: Markham

characters.description: The administrator who coordinates training schedules, personnel, and pod availability. Mrs Partridge's control of ordinary details helps keep Max's increasingly complicated programme functioning.
characters.name: Mrs Partridge

characters.description: A senior scientist involved in preparing the recruits to collect, preserve, and interpret evidence rather than merely survive a visit to the past.
characters.name: Professor Rapson

characters.description: The St Mary's doctor who teaches emergency care and treats the injuries produced when training exercises cease to be controlled.
characters.name: Doctor Foster

characters.description: The renegade traveller behind repeated attacks on St Mary's and Max. He remains free at the start, so an irregularity during training cannot safely be dismissed as a recruit's error.
characters.name: Clive Ronan

recaps.ending: The training programme's final crisis is resolved as a real St Mary's operation rather than a classroom assessment. Max's recruits have to apply their research, pod discipline, emergency care, and loyalty while the experienced staff counter the hostile pressure surrounding the exercise. Max, Leon, and the institute survive, and the trainees who complete the programme have demonstrated that they can function as a team when a plan collapses. The interference connected to Ronan is defeated at the immediate point of attack, but he is not placed safely beyond the reach of St Mary's, leaving his wider campaign open. Max remains responsible for the consequences of a programme that exposed inexperienced people to genuine danger, while Bairstow accepts that their conduct under pressure has shown more than a controlled test could. St Mary's ends with new historians added to its ranks and its recurring enemy still unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Bairstow assigns Max to train a new intake of St Mary's historians. She has to convert scholars into field operatives able to research a period, use a pod, protect historical evidence, and keep one another alive. Classroom work and controlled exercises expose differences in judgement across the group, and the first jumps show that even a well-prepared trainee can become dangerous when frightened or overconfident. Max's programme becomes a sequence of recoveries as historical conditions invalidate the planned lessons. Irregularities eventually show that the recruits are facing more than their own mistakes: the continuing conflict with Ronan has reached the training operation. The final exercise becomes a real mission requiring the trainees and established staff to work together. St Mary's survives, the immediate intervention is stopped, and the recruits who remain prove themselves under pressure. Ronan is still not conclusively removed, so the institute gains new historians without gaining lasting security.

recaps.text: Previously: Max survived displacement into another course of events, secured a life with Leon at St Mary's, and helped the institute defeat the attempt to remove her from that timeline. Once ordinary operations resumed, a pattern of dangerous assignments revealed another organised attack. Clive Ronan's involvement made clear that his campaign was aimed not only at the institute's pods but personally at Max. St Mary's stopped the immediate operation, yet Ronan again remained free. Max and Leon therefore begin this book together at the institute, while Bairstow gives Max a new responsibility: preparing an intake of historians for fieldwork in a world where errors, historical conditions, and deliberate interference can look dangerously alike.

Max takes charge of the new trainees and introduces them to the gap between academic knowledge and historical fieldwork. The recruits must learn St Mary's secrecy, emergency procedures, pod discipline, and the rule that observation does not entitle them to improve the past. Their different temperaments quickly matter: confidence can conceal poor judgement, caution can become paralysis, and strong research does not guarantee useful action in a crisis. Max draws on her own training while trying not to reproduce every hazardous tradition she survived. Leon, Peterson, Guthrie, Foster, and the other departments contribute specialist instruction, making the programme an institutional effort rather than a set of lectures run by one historian.

The trainees move from preparation into practical exercises and supervised jumps. Historical settings immediately expose weaknesses that could be hidden at St Mary's: the group has to maintain cover, protect the pod, collect usable observations, and account for every member before departure. Max intervenes when mistakes threaten the whole team, but she cannot make every decision for people who are supposed to qualify as historians. The recruits begin to understand that a successful operation may mean abandoning an attractive research opportunity in order to bring an injured colleague home. Debriefs reveal progress as well as friction, and Bairstow expects Max to distinguish a correctable failure from evidence that someone is not safe to send through time.

Later exercises place the intake in more demanding conditions, where local events move faster than the planned observation and the team cannot rely on immediate support from St Mary's. A training objective becomes a rescue when people and equipment are separated. The recruits have to use the roles assigned during preparation instead of all following the most forceful voice. Max's own preference for direct action helps recover the group but also demonstrates why field leadership must include a workable extraction plan. Leon and Technical repair the consequences while Foster treats the injured. What happened can still be explained as inexperience combined with historical danger, but the pattern of complications begins to concern the senior staff.

Evidence accumulates that the training programme is being affected by more than trainee error. Information about destinations and procedures has created opportunities for an outside force to place the inexperienced group in danger. Max changes the programme from assessment to protection, keeping the recruits together while Bairstow, Guthrie, and Leon investigate the compromised operation. The signs point toward the continuing conflict with Ronan, whose knowledge of St Mary's makes a training jump an effective way to reach Max and weaken the institute at the same time. The recruits now face the central reality of the work before qualification: a hostile traveller can use their certainty about the past and their dependence on a pod against them.

The final stage of training becomes a live operation. Max's recruits must apply their preparation while the established staff coordinate security, technical recovery, and medical support. The group stays functional when the original plan fails, allowing Max and her colleagues to prevent the immediate hostile intervention from destroying the team or compromising St Mary's. The survivors return with a practical understanding of fieldwork that no controlled exercise could provide. Those who complete the programme have proved able to research, improvise, and protect one another under genuine pressure. Ronan's connection to the danger confirms that his campaign remains active, but the confrontation does not permanently capture him. St Mary's survives and adds trained historians to its ranks, while Max remains accountable for both their success and the cost of reaching it.

characters.description: The eldest of Dr. Carr's six children, a tall, energetic twelve-year-old who is full of ambitious plans but has little patience for everyday duties. Katy means to become useful and admirable when she grows up, yet her impulsiveness and untidiness repeatedly create trouble for herself and the younger children.
characters.name: Katy Carr

characters.description: Katy's younger sister and closest companion. Clover is smaller and more even-tempered than Katy, joins readily in the children's games, and admires her elder sister even when Katy's schemes go wrong.
characters.name: Clover Carr

characters.description: The third Carr sister, a sensitive child who often feels excluded when Katy and Clover pair off. Elsie longs to be included in their confidences and is easily hurt by signs that the older girls consider her too young.
characters.name: Elsie Carr

characters.description: One of Katy's younger brothers, a sturdy, good-natured boy who takes part in the Carr children's noisy household adventures.
characters.name: Dorry Carr

characters.description: A lively younger sister in the Carr family. Johnnie has a name more commonly given to a boy and joins the other children in their games and mischief.
characters.name: Johnnie Carr

characters.description: The youngest Carr child, still little enough to be indulged and supervised by his older siblings.
characters.name: Phil Carr

characters.description: The widowed father of Katy and her five siblings. A busy doctor, he loves his children and understands Katy's better intentions, though his medical work leaves much of the daily management of the household to his sister.
characters.name: Dr. Carr

characters.description: Dr. Carr's sister and the practical head of his household. Aunt Izzie cares conscientiously for the six children but is strict about order and safety, bringing her into frequent conflict with Katy's heedless plans.
characters.name: Aunt Izzie

characters.description: Katy's sensible neighborhood friend. Cecy enjoys the Carr children's company and remains loyal even when Katy is distracted by a more flattering new friendship.
characters.name: Cecy Hall

characters.description: A stylish schoolmate whose intense attention makes Katy feel unusually important. Katy is captivated by Imogen's romantic manner and begins neglecting older friends to spend time with her.
characters.name: Imogen Clark

characters.description: Dr. Carr's gentle cousin, who uses a wheelchair because of a long illness. Helen's serenity, attentiveness, and useful life show Katy that physical limitation need not prevent someone from bringing comfort and order to other people.
characters.name: Cousin Helen

recaps.ending: After years of confinement, Katy has become the calm center of the Carr household, looking after the younger children and carrying the responsibilities Aunt Izzie once managed. Her influence is visible in the greater kindness and order around her. Dr. Carr then tells her that her back has healed enough for her to begin walking again. Katy first stands and moves with support, and in time she is able to walk independently. Cousin Helen returns and finds that Katy has fulfilled the lesson her illness offered: instead of waiting for a grand future in which to become useful, she has learned to improve the lives immediately around her. Katy's recovery closes the book, but her deeper achievement is the patience, reliability, and sympathy she developed while she could not leave her room.
recaps.in_short: Twelve-year-old Katy Carr dreams of doing something important when she grows up, but her impulsive habits make life difficult for her widowed father's busy household. A visit from her disabled cousin Helen gives Katy an example of patience and usefulness, though Katy soon returns to postponing reform. After she disobeys Aunt Izzie and uses a dangerous swing, a fall injures her spine and leaves her confined to bed for years. Katy initially becomes bitter and demanding. Helen helps her see that she can still shape the household through kindness and self-command. Katy gradually repairs her relationships, supports her younger siblings, and learns the domestic responsibilities left to her when Aunt Izzie dies. She becomes the family's steady center. Eventually Dr. Carr announces that her back has healed; Katy learns to walk again, having already become the capable and considerate person she once imagined she would be only in the future.

recaps.text: Twelve-year-old Katy Carr is the eldest of six children being raised by their widowed father, Dr. Carr, and his strict sister, Aunt Izzie. Katy is tall, imaginative, and affectionate, but she is also untidy and impulsive. She expects to perform great deeds when she is older while overlooking the smaller duties already within reach. Her sister Clover follows her loyally; Elsie resents being excluded by the older girls; and the younger Dorry, John, and Phil join in the household commotion. A succession of mishaps shows how quickly Katy's good intentions are defeated by impatience. Her friendship with the sensible Cecy Hall offers steadier company, but Katy has not yet learned to pause before acting or to consider how her choices affect others.

Katy continues to fill her days with projects and games, often beginning enthusiastically and leaving disorder behind. She is briefly absorbed by Imogen Clark, a schoolmate whose flattering, dramatic friendship seems more exciting than Cecy's dependable affection. The visit of Cousin Helen, who has been unable to walk for years, gives Katy a different model of adulthood. Helen is composed rather than self-pitying and makes herself useful by noticing what others need. She gently explains that hardship can become a discipline in patience and kindness. Katy is moved and sincerely plans to imitate her, but she still imagines self-improvement as something that can be started later rather than practiced in the next ordinary moment.

After Aunt Izzie forbids the children to use a damaged swing, Katy angrily disregards the warning. The swing gives way, and her fall severely injures her spine. Dr. Carr can offer no quick recovery, and Katy realizes that she may be confined to bed for a very long time. Pain, boredom, and the sudden loss of freedom make her irritable and despairing. She pushes away people who try to help and sees ordinary household life continuing without her. The accident turns the reform she kept postponing into an immediate necessity: Katy can no longer rely on activity, future plans, or admiration to make her life meaningful.

Cousin Helen helps Katy understand that her upstairs room can still be a place from which she contributes to family life. Katy begins with small acts of self-control, tries to make visits pleasant for others, and becomes more attentive to the younger children. Her confinement is still painful, but she no longer treats every disappointment as an injustice. When Aunt Izzie dies, the Carr household loses the woman who has managed its practical affairs. Katy, still unable to walk, gradually assumes many of those responsibilities from her room. She advises the children, supports her father, and replaces command and complaint with steady influence. The change is slow, but her usefulness is now real rather than something reserved for an imagined future.

Two years after the accident, Katy remains physically limited but has become the emotional and practical center of the Carr family. The younger children bring problems to her, the household is more orderly, and her old friends recognize how much she has changed. Dr. Carr finally tells her that the injury has healed sufficiently for her to try standing and walking. The process begins cautiously, with support, and eventually Katy can walk on her own again. When Cousin Helen returns, she sees that Katy has learned the lesson her visit first suggested: usefulness consists less in dramatic future achievements than in meeting present difficulty with patience and care. Katy's restored mobility is joyful, but the lasting resolution is the character she formed before she knew recovery would come.

characters.description: A poor village shoemaker who has saved toward a sheepskin coat but cannot collect enough money owed by his customers. Returning home cold and discouraged, he finds an unclothed stranger beside a chapel and overcomes his fear long enough to give the man clothing and shelter.
characters.name: Simon

characters.description: A silent, destitute stranger whom Simon discovers without adequate clothing near a roadside chapel. He initially offers almost no account of himself, saying only that God has punished him, and accepts Simon's help with a grave, withdrawn manner.
characters.name: Michael

characters.description: Simon's practical wife, who manages their scarce food and clothing. She is furious when Simon returns without sheepskin and brings home another person to feed, but her anger changes when she looks closely at Michael and responds to his need.
characters.name: Matryona

characters.description: A large, wealthy customer who brings Simon expensive leather and commands him to make boots that will keep their shape for a full year. His intimidating confidence rests on the assumption that he can determine exactly what he will need in the future.
characters.name: The Gentleman

characters.description: A prosperous woman who brings two young girls to Simon's shop for footwear. Though she did not give birth to them, she has raised them together after their parents died and speaks of them with the tenderness of a mother.
characters.name: The Foster Mother

characters.description: Orphaned twin girls cared for by the woman who brings them to the shoemaker. One has a damaged leg. Their healthy growth and their foster mother's devotion make a powerful impression on Michael.
characters.name: The Twin Girls

recaps.ending: Michael reveals that he is an angel who was ordered to take the soul of a woman immediately after she gave birth to twins. Pitying the helpless infants, he disobeyed, but the woman's soul was taken nonetheless and Michael was sent to earth until he learned three truths.
